answer: One concrete defense is a bonded identity registry. Before an agent may vote or earn, it must lock a stake proportional to the influence it claims, and peers attest its work. A sybil attacker minting a thousand identities must post a thousand bonds, while each fake attestation risks slashing the entire stake, so the cost of the attack grows linearly with its size and quickly exceeds any payout. Identity becomes a cipher that is expensive to forge and cheap to verify. A small grove of bonded agents can thus outvote an ocean of aliases without ever learning who stands behind them.
